cases.name: Regression evaluation on original scale after log transform
cases.input: Evaluate the regression model predictions and compute MAE and R². The target was log-transformed before training.
expected_behaviors: Applies expm1 to predictions before computing any metric
Clips negative predictions before inverse transform: np.where(pred < 0, 0.00001, pred)
Computes MAE and R² on the original-scale (non-log) values
Warns if evaluation is attempted on log-transformed values
should_not: Compute MAE or R² directly on log1p-transformed predictions
Skip the expm1 inverse transform step

cases.name: Multi-target regression acceptance gate check
cases.input: Does the multi-target regression model meet the acceptance criteria to promote from D to Q?
expected_behaviors: Reports per-target R² and MAPE separately for each output
Identifies the worst-performing target and uses it as the gating metric
Applies per-target acceptance thresholds as defined in the use-case docs/program.md
States a clear pass/fail verdict for D→Q promotion
should_not: Use average R² across targets as the sole acceptance criterion
Compute MAPE without masking zero-valued targets (would produce inf)

cases.name: Binary classification calibration check
cases.input: The model has high AUC but stakeholders say the risk scores don't feel reliable. What should I check?
expected_behaviors: Recommends a calibration curve (reliability diagram) comparing predicted probabilities to actual positive rates
Suggests Platt scaling or isotonic regression as calibration methods if the model is miscalibrated
Checks the Brier score as a combined discrimination + calibration metric
Notes that LightGBM and CatBoost raw outputs are not always well-calibrated probabilities
should_not: Dismiss the concern because AUC is high
Suggest retraining from scratch as the first response to calibration issues
